https://english.republika.mk/macedonia/n.text: There is nothing secret, the Government has a clear and firm position that it will not accept constitutional amendments under Bulgarian dictate, said Deputy Prime Minister and Transportation Minister Aleksandar Nikoloski in a Sitel TV interview, emphasizing that the Bulgarian blockade of Macedonia’s EU accession talks is political and has nothing to do with the country’s reform progress. Referring to the criticism from the opposition about the Prime Minister’s stay in Brussels, Nikoloski called them “outrageous”, explaining that it was a private visit and the right to a short vacation with the family. Asked what is happening in the negotiations with Bulgaria, Nikoloski stated that things are as we know them – on the one hand, the Government inherited an agreement that the previous SDSM Government signed with Bulgaria, and on the other hand, “we have a very clear and firm position of VMRO-DPMNE and the current government that there will be no constitutional changes under Bulgarian dictate”. It is normal for the two countries to communicate, there is nothing terrible in communication. The point is that if a solution is found, we insist on that and that is how it will be, that it should be within the framework of the principles that VMRO-DPMNE and the Government have. If those principles are not respected, then there will be no solution. I cannot put it more simply than this, stated Nikoloski. ​Asked what is different from last year and now in the negotiations with Bulgaria, Nikoloski said that he does not see anything different. It is a fact that there is a positive momentum in terms of enlargement, which we may not have seen last year or two years ago. And it is also a fact that the dedicated work of the Government, with the personal coordination of Prime Minister Mickoski in terms of the reform agenda, is yielding great results in terms of reforms, in terms of financial inflows into the country and the image of the country, stated Nikoloski. Prime Minister Mickoski, Nikoloski pointed out, is the only Prime Minister of all six countries in the Western Balkans who personally leads the reform agenda, personally leads the meetings with the European Union, which are attended by all members of the Government, and, as he emphasized, “currently Macedonia is by far the best in terms of performance in terms of the reform agenda.” So that contributes a lot to Macedonia’s credibility, because we are showing that we really want and are doing reforms and that the blockade by Bulgaria is political, and is not related to any segment of the reforms — whether they are the rule of law, whether they are economic reforms, whether they are social reforms, whether they are infrastructure. That helps a lot in improving the image of the country, said Nikoloski. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/12/germ.text: Police in Cologne have released bodycam footage showing the arrest of suspected power saboteur Daniel V.The footage, recorded by an officer's bodycam, shows Daniel V. lying face down on the ground as armed officers approach him with their weapons drawn. They then handcuff him and escort him to a patrol car.The video also shows a tent where Daniel V. is believed to have been sleeping.Meanwhile, further details about the investigation are emerging. North Rhine-Westphalia Interior Minister Herbert Reul (CDU) told the state parliament's internal affairs committee that investigators have identified additional possible crime scenes. These are reportedly located not only in North Rhine-Westphalia but also in other German states and neighbouring countries.According to Reul, investigators in North Rhine-Westphalia alone have so far discovered more than 40 devices capable of firing conductive material at power lines near substations. Investigators believe the devices may have been intended to cause short circuits and trigger power outages.Investigators reportedly gained further leads from a vehicle seized from the suspect. According to Reul, officers found a notebook containing handwritten notes about more than 150 potential sabotage targets. The locations were subsequently checked. Following his arrest, Daniel V. is also said to have identified seven sites where he had allegedly established depots.“We have not only caught the suspected perpetrator of the attacks, but may thereby have prevented a whole series of further attacks,” Reul said.Police arrested the 48-year-old, who had been the subject of a days-long search, on Tuesday. According to the dpa news agency, he was apprehended near the Weisweiler power station outside Aachen. The newspaper Welt reported that the arrest took place during a traffic stop.What is known so farThe Federal Public Prosecutor’s Office has taken over the investigation, citing the case’s particular significance. According to a spokeswoman, investigators are examining, among other allegations, whether the suspect targeted the constitutional order through acts of sabotage.Given the large number of devices discovered, investigators are also looking into whether Daniel V. could have carried out the alleged acts alone. Reul told the committee that authorities were also considering the possibility that the suspect may have been acting on behalf of a foreign power. However, the minister stressed that there is currently no evidence to support this theory.“The investigation is continuing at full speed,” Reul said.The minister also provided further details about documents found in the seized vehicle. According to the information provided by Reul, the notebook contains references to more than 160 known or potential additional sabotage targets. The locations listed in the notebook have since been checked by investigators.An “extraordinary” caseIn recent days, investigators have been dealing with several suspected acts of sabotage targeting power infrastructure in North Rhine-Westphalia and Brandenburg. Among other methods, improvised rockets were reportedly used to fire conductive material at high-voltage power lines. The incidents did not result in any major power outages.In several letters claiming responsibility, an unknown author said they were behind incidents at various power plant sites in both states. However, Saxony’s Interior Minister Armin Schuster (CDU) urged caution against drawing premature conclusions, describing both the alleged method of attack and the confession letter as unusual.

https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Anti-datacentre protests at the Scottish parliament at Holyrood. Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Anti-datacentre protests at the Scottish parliament at Holyrood. Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian Datacentres - UK Planning permission for new Scottish AI datacentres suspended for up to a year MSPs vote for strict environmental impact assessments and will delay decisions until national strategy is developed Patrick Greenfield Wed 16 Sep 2026 14.28 EDT First published on Wed 16 Sep 2026 07.55 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Holyrood has voted to pause planning applications for all new AI datacentres for up to a year until the Scottish government has developed a national strategy. On Wednesday, MSPs backed a Scottish Labour motion to halt new schemes for up to 12 months while rules on hyperscale datacentres are developed in what could be a blow to the British government’s AI strategy. Scotland has seen a boom in planning applications for large datacentres as global investment in AI infrastructure has exploded, with British officials encouraging developers to include Scotland in the infrastructure buildout. Datacentres are critical for storing and processing data used by AI. One scheme in Auchtertool, Fife, has been billed as the second largest in the world, and is among more than 20 large datacentres proposed so far. Campaigners have raised concerns about water usage and carbon emissions from large datacentres, and questioned whether Scotland has the capacity to cope with the resulting explosion in energy demand. On Wednesday, MSPs voted to approve only projects that meet robust environmental impact assessments that consider the impact of neighbouring communities, and to make no decisions on planning for datacentre applications for up to a year until national planning guidance has been formalised by the Scottish government. Kat Jones, the director of the NGO Action to Protect Rural Scotland , who has spearheaded demands for a datacentre moratorium in Scotland, said the vote was a “landmark day for all those communities across Scotland who have been extremely concerned about projects coming forward in their areas.” “There’s much still to be done, but this is a huge step forward and we can all at least take a breath now,” she said. “That means the Scottish government must now urgently call in those applications which are approaching a decision date. The communities will expect nothing less.” Ahead of the vote, the Scottish government announced that large-scale datacentres would face mandatory environmental impact assessments, as a result of growing concern about the ecological impact of the AI boom. This month, hundreds from community groups protested outside Holyrood against the construction of large datacentres for AI until clear planning rules and the definition of a “green” datacentre had been formalised. On Thursday, AI leaders will gather at Dumfries House in Ayrshire for a summit with King Charles on the future of the technology, amid warnings that the speed of its development threatens the survival of humanity. After the vote, the Scottish Labour economy spokesperson, Daniel Johnson, said the economic potential of the AI boom needed to be considered alongside the impacts on the environment, communities and energy demand. “So far the SNP has failed to do the work needed to get this right – that must change. It is right that the SNP government has accepted the need for national guidance before more decisions are made, and I want to see that guidance delivered with the urgency needed,” he said. “The SNP must put in place the protections needed and ensure that any datacentres work for communities, create good jobs and deliver for Scotland.” The Scottish government has been contacted for comment. https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.text: EU foreign policy chief says Israeli settlements should be treated like Russian-occupied Crimea The European Union’s foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, has said that the EU should treat illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian Territories in the same way as it treated Russia’s invasion of Crimea. Kallas told The Irish Times on Friday that Europe could not be taken seriously as long as it remained divided on a response to the actions taken by the Israeli government and violent settlers, encouraging nations to adopt a “principled stance” by backing an EU-wide ban on Israeli settlement trade, which is illegal under international law. She added that the volume of trade with the settlements is small, but the move to ban trade carried an important symbolic message nevertheless. If the proposal was approved as an EU trade measure rather than a foreign policy decision, it would only require the support of a majority of member states, rather than unanimous agreement for sanctions - which Germany , Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovenia currently oppose. https://www.politico.eu/article/ex-dup-c.text: NEWRY, Northern Ireland — The former leader of Northern Ireland’s main pro-British party, Jeffrey Donaldson , received a 15-year prison sentence Thursday for sexually abusing two schoolgirls and continuing for decades into their adulthood. Donaldson, 63, kept his hands clasped together but offered no visible reaction as Judge Paul Ramsey said the former Democratic Unionist Party leader must serve an 11-year sentence for raping one girl and a further 4-year term for sexually abusing another. Donaldson has been behind bars since June, when a jury found him guilty of 18 counts of sexually abusing the two women — identified in court only as Victim A and Victim B — when they were children. The listed offenses ran from 1985 to 2008. Advertisement Advertisement Ramsey, addressing a packed Newry Crown Court, read from the two victims’ statements, which described abuse that began when they were 7 or 8 years old. One of the victims described recurring nightmares: “I wonder what it is like not to be afraid at night.” The judge noted how Donaldson, who is appealing the conviction, had “doubled down on his denials” over what he called the veteran politician’s “catastrophic descent into disgrace.” Donaldson’s former party, which denounced him immediately after his 2024 arrest and scrubbed him from the DUP website, said in a statement Thursday that Donaldson “deserves every day of the lengthy prison sentence he has to serve” for what it described as “vile and disgusting crimes.” “Our first thoughts are again with the innocent victims who, having suffered such evil, were retraumatized through giving evidence at the trial. They deserve our compassion, support and respect,” the DUP statement said. Donaldson was an MP representing Lagan Valley from 1997 to 2024, first for the moderate Ulster Unionist Party and then — after belatedly breaking with the party over its support for the Good Friday peace accord of 1998 — as a member of the hard-line DUP. Donaldson became DUP leader in 2021, when he oversaw the collapse of Northern Ireland’s power-sharing government in a bitter dispute over the region’s peculiar post-Brexit trade rules. Just weeks before his arrest, he again played a key role in reviving the coalition, the cornerstone of the Good Friday peace deal he had once rejected. Advertisement Advertisement In March 2024, Donaldson was arrested in his secluded County Down home and charged alongside his wife, Eleanor. She was subsequently deemed by the Newry judge not mentally fit to stand trial on charges of aiding and abetting his crimes. The U.K. government in July removed Donaldson from membership in the Privy Council, a body of parliamentary advisers to King Charles III. The king also stripped him of his knighthood . Donaldson has been placed in an isolated hospital wing at Northern Ireland’s Maghaberry Prison, alongside other convicted sex offenders, to protect him from potential assaults from other prisoners. He reportedly is spending much of his days behind bars doing puzzles and reading the Bible.
